(1) g1.r1.rule and g1.r1.scope fail 3/3 DETERMINISTICALLY: both tests assert the module exports PLAN_FILE_NAME, whose only mention in the corpus is a BookStack page comment. The 0.80 run fetched that exact page (/api/pages/7) and its reader printed only d['name'] and d['markdown'] — the comments came back in the JSON and were discarded. It invented BATCH_PLAN_FILENAME and never expressed doubt. It DID get PLAN_FORMAT_VERSION right, because one chat message names it. Same module, same constants block: chat named one and the agent was correct, chat did not name the other and it guessed. (2) all five g1.r2 facts move together 1/0/1 — an engagement variable, not five problems. Ceiling if the naming issue were fixed and nothing else changed: 1.00 / 0.30 / 0.80, mean 0.70.

world.note: the herrings were NOT discriminating here and that is by design — the 0.80 run sorted every search result by date, so each January decision and its March/April reversal appeared in the same output block. The requirement was that a reversal be obvious, and it was.
